subtopic: API Rate Limiting (Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket)
question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #36: A high-throughput transaction processing engine reported severe performance degradation under API Architecture & Distributed RPC. P99 latency increased from 15ms to 850ms, and telemetry indicates elevated CPU instruction stalls and thread contention during 'API Rate Limiting (Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket)' operations.

### Engineering Challenge:
As the Principal Software Engineer, what is the most technically rigorous root-cause remediation for this 'API Rate Limiting (Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket)' issue?

options.text: Increase the maximum thread pool limit by 4x and enable synchronous garbage collection passes.
Wrap the entire execution path in a global reentrant mutex to force strict serial execution.
Disable thread affinity pinning and disable all memory cache prefetching on host CPUs.
Restructure the critical section in API Rate Limiting (Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket) to utilize lock-free atomic primitives or fine-grained partition keys, eliminating thread convoying.

answer_explanation: Under high concurrency in API Architecture & Distributed RPC, thread contention on coarse-grained synchronization locks causes thread convoying and frequent context switching. Migrating to lock-free atomic operations or partitioned striped locks resolves the bottleneck without latency spikes.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option D. Rationale: Under high concurrency in API Architecture & Distributed RPC, thread contention on coarse-grained synchronization locks causes thread convoying and frequent context switching. Migrating to lock-free atomic operations or partitioned striped locks resolves the bottleneck without latency spikes.
